Great 4k capture of this incredible revival in previews shortly before opening! Fairly severe camera fog within the first 25 minutes, some washout and obstruction from heads in wideshots, but little to no wandering throughout. Due to the nature of the thrust stage and the fact that this video was taken from the side, occasionally actors have their backs turned to the audience and facial expressions are missed. Includes bows.

Alex's first performance in the final week. Second to last performance of the production overall. With audience that were not much less energetic than the derniere. 1080p HD, steady clear view from the middle with some minor obstruction on the bottom right that doesn't really block anything. With a very shaky curtain call and full audio. Hope you enjoy.

Okay 4K capture of this glitzy, modernized interpretation of Romeo and Juliet. Shot over and around one very annoying head, which obstructs the action quite often, and there are moments of blind shooting where the camera focuses on the wrong thing. But when I managed to get closeups, they can be quite nice. Moderate washout in wideshots. Due to the nature of the production taking place in the round, some moments are not captured from the clearest angle. Audio of the intermission music performed by the cast is captured, though video is not. As a general warning, the video contains moments of intense strobing lights: rough timestamps (07:15-09:00), (46:45-47:45), (1:04:45-1:05:30).

Excellent 4K capture of this year’s Best Play winner! Minor obstruction is present in the first and second act but is no longer present after intermission. Some moments of wandering and unfocusing, first ten minutes are mostly wideshot. Heads are sometimes cut off if actors stand very far back in the recording booth. One or two short blackouts. The crowd is loud and enthusiastic, which is encouraged, but does mean some moments are difficult to hear. Includes curtain call, audio is fed from external source.
Beautiful capture, occasionally Jamie-focused. Includes audio of bows and playout

Great capture of this excellent show! The first 30-ish minutes have obstruction on the bottom left of the stage and sometimes further center when they lean to the side; some action is missed because of this but it’s worked around as best as possible. The rest is mostly unobstructed. Otherwise shot very well in a great mix of close-ups, mediums, and wide-shots. Some wandering, shaking, and re-adjusting throughout. A couple of brief dropouts. Audio is patched in from an external source; my audio recorder scrapes up against my bag a LOT in this recording and it is often audible. Some grain when the show gets very dark. Overall a great capture.
